title: Cap. 6 Arg. 4 open: Contrary inconveniences—uneven grace pinned on the human obstacle
pass_a_gloss: This same thing can be proved from the manifest inconveniences with which the contrary opinion is pressed. For if by the death of Christ it has been universally obtained that God by the decree itself, or by a certain law of congruity, is bound, as far as in him lies, to grant to all and each human beings the grace of evangelical preaching and of inward sanctification, then it will follow that the primary reason why this one in fact becomes a partaker of both graces, that one does not, is situated in this: that this one by opposing an obstacle has repelled this grace, or has wholly hindered it from being offered, while that one has neither repelled nor hindered it. The adversaries do not flee this consequence. For they do not reduce the discrimination of evangelical calling and of saving grace denied or granted into the mere will of God, but into diverse conditions or dispositions considered on the human side. So Corvinus, Against Tilenus, page 489: Although God does not preach the word of the cross everywhere, still he is ready to preach it to all those who duly subject themselves to the ministry of the law, that is, who follow the light of the natural law that is vigorous even in the hearts of the Gentiles. Differing on natural gifts, page 118, he says that God left these gifts to the nations so that if indeed according to God's intention they used those gifts, they would be led to glorifying God according to the measure of their knowledge, and to Christ and the knowledge of him; but on the contrary they would be left in their ignorance if they held down in injustice the truth they had. Here he openly hangs evangelical calling on the use or abuse of natural gifts.
pass_b_english: The same point can be proved from the plain inconveniences that press the contrary view. If by Christ's death it has been universally obtained that God is bound—by the decree itself, or by some law of congruity—to grant, as far as in him lies, to every human being the grace of gospel preaching and of inward sanctification, then the chief reason why one person in fact shares both graces and another does not will lie here: that one has thrust up an obstacle and pushed the grace away, or has blocked it from being offered at all, while the other has neither pushed it away nor blocked it. Our opponents do not shrink from that consequence. They do not reduce the difference between evangelical calling and saving grace denied or granted to God's bare will, but to different conditions or dispositions on the human side. So Corvinus against Tilenus, page 489: though God does not preach the word of the cross everywhere, he is still ready to preach it to all who duly submit themselves to the ministry of the law—that is, who follow the light of the natural law alive even in Gentile hearts. Writing on natural gifts, page 118, he says God left those gifts to the nations so that if they used them according to God's intention, they would be led to glorify God in the measure of their knowledge, and on to Christ and the knowledge of him; but if they held down in injustice the truth they had, they would be left in their ignorance. Here he openly hangs the gospel call on the use or abuse of natural gifts.
source_text: Hoc idem probari potest ex incommodis manifestis quibus urgetur sententia contraria. Nam si hoc morte Christi sit universaliter impetratum, ut Deus ex ipso decreto, sive lege quadam congruitatis teneatur, quantum in se est, omnibus & singulis hominibus gratiam Evangelicae praedicationis atque internae sanctificationis concedere, tum sequetur, rationem primariam cur hic de facto fiat particeps utriusque gratiae, ille non fiat, in eo sitam, quod hic obice opposito hanc gratiam repulerit, aut ne offeretur omnino impedierit, ille nec repulerit nec impedierit. Hanc consequentiam non refugiunt adversarii. Nam vocationis Evangelicae & gratiae salutiferae negatae aut concessae discrimen non in meram Dei voluntatem reducunt, sed in conditiones sive dispositiones diversas ex parte hominum consideratas. Sic Corvinus, Contra Tilen. pag. 489. Deus licet ubique verbum crucis non praedicet, omnibus tamen iis illud praedicare paratus est, qui ministerio legis sese debite subjiciunt, hoc est, qui sequuntur lucem legis naturalis etiam in Ethnicorum cordibus vigentis. De donis naturalibus differens, pag. 118. dicit, Deum haec dona gentilibus reliquisse, ut siquidem secundum Dei intentionem istis donis uterentur, ad Deum pro mensura suae cognitionis glorificandum, ad Christum ipsiusque cognitionem ducerentur: contra vero, in sua ignorantia relinquerentur, si veritatem quam habebant in injustitia detinerent. Hic aperte suspendit vocationem Evangelicam ex usu aut abusu donorum naturalium.
